text.p: These are the main stories in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- The government will soon amend the income tax law, which will mean Lithuanians paid abroad to pay 20 percent income tax at home.
- Parliament rejected the initiative of the Centre Union to amend the constitution to allow Lithuanians living abroad to stand as president.
- The agricultural fair AgroBalt'97 opened in Vilnius. The event attracts more and more participants each year.
- The head of the customs department told parliament that his office improved customs collection and the budget received 168.86 million litas in revenues in April, a 65 percent rise.
- The director general of Lithuanian Airlines Stasys Dailydka was sacked from his post on Tuesday. The transport ministry appointed Stasys Jarmalavichius, 45.
RESPUBLIKA
- President Algirdas Brazauskas hosted a reception for Lithuanian and foreign journalists to mark Free Press day.
- Brazauskas said he would like to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin if an agreement on border delimitation between the two countries is intialed.
- Business Eastern Europe doubts the sucessful privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom.
LIETUVOS AIDAS
- The social insurance fund SODRA with annual turnover of 3.5 billion litas was 30 million litas under planned revenue every month this year.
- Defence minister Cheslovas Stankevichius left for Denmark to take part in a meeting of the defence ministers of Poland, Germany and Denmark.
- Parliament decided that in an emergency the state can take over control of the Klaipeda and Butinge oil terminals.
VERSLO ZINIOS

- Ragutis brewery, 51 percent owned by Czech Pilzner Urquell, is expecting 11 million litas investment, two million litas this year, to upgrade its production lines. Ragutis has 11 percent of the country's beer market.
- Jim Beam Brands Worldwide Tom Willen said it expects to boost expots of Jim Beam to Lithuania by 15-20 percent.
- Milk processing companies bought 208,000 tonnes of milk, a 10 percent increase during the same period last year.
-- Andrius Vilkancas, Vilnius newsroom +370 2 22 35 17
